rationale.streamIdleTimeoutSeconds: How long the video-creation model may go quiet mid-response before the authoring run gives up. The request is streamed, so this bounds the gap between chunks rather than the whole generation: a reasoning model streams a long reasoning phase before the composition, and a 180 second bound on the whole response timed out the production one-sentence path. Six minutes of complete silence is a service that has stopped answering, not one that is thinking.
rationale.wholeResponseIsNotBoundedHere: There is a separate ceiling on the whole authoring child, enforced by the native side, and it surfaces as its own outcome (authoring_timed_out). Restating it here would let the App tell the user one number while the process obeyed another.
rationale.declaredHere: The number was a literal in agent.py, and that is why the App could not name it. 'You waited longer than we allow' is not something a user can act on: it does not say whether the wait was long enough to mean anything, or whether retrying is worth it. Writing '6 分' into the sentence instead would have created a hand-copied second version that nothing checks, so the first tuning of this budget would have made the App state a figure the Executor no longer used. Both sides read this file, exactly as they already do for motion-storyboard-duration.v1.
rationale.changing: Raising or lowering it means editing this file alone. The Executor picks it up at import and the sentence on the card is recomposed from it; enforcedBy fails if either side reintroduces a literal.
rationale.thinking: What is declared is the *saving*, never the absolute wait, and that is a deliberate correction. The measurement is in **model seconds** — one round trip — while everything else the studio says about authoring is **end-to-end wall clock** (MOTION_AUTHORING_MEASURED, 136-178s measured in T83). demo-sprint-roadmap.md records the rule that came out of T92: the two are different units and swapping one for the other is worse than leaving the old number alone. An earlier version of this printed 42 next to a card already reading 编排加渲染最长约, which is both units on one screen. The saving is the one figure that carries across, because turning reasoning off removes the same phase from both. Four paired observations against the real model with the real authoring prompt, 2026-07-28/29: reasoning on 40.5 / 41.7 / 51.0 / 69.8s, off 8.5 / 9.9 / 10.9 / 23.5s. Median 46.4 against 10.4 gives 36 typical; the extremes a caller could actually meet are 40.5-23.5 = 17 and 69.8-8.5 = 61. The spread is wider than the middle, which is why a point estimate is not offered on its own — the fourth pair came from the real-chain verification and was itself outside the range the first three implied.
